title: THE WISEST MAN… LOST HIS HEART.
paragraphs: THE WISEST MAN… LOST HIS HEART.

Not to ignorance.
Not to war.
Not to poverty.
Because this story doesn’t begin with rebellion. It begins with brilliance.

He was the son of King David.
Chosen by God.
Anointed for greatness.
When he first took the throne, he didn’t ask for gold.
“Give Your servant an understanding heart…” (1 Kings 3:9)
God gave him a mind like a blade of light. Nations traveled miles just to hear him speak. The queen of Sheba left breathless at his glory.

He built the Temple of the Lord in Jerusalem.
Gold shimmered. Incense rose. The presence of God filled the house.
“King Solomon loved many foreign women…” (1 Kings 11:1)

Seven hundred wives.
Three hundred concubines.
And the text says it plainly:

He still wrote proverbs.
Still governed wisely.
Still looked successful.
Some scholars interpret Solomon’s fall as gradual political alliances through marriage. Others see it as unchecked appetite masquerading as diplomacy. Either way—the result was the same.

Shrines to Ashtoreth.
Offerings to Molech.

The man who built God’s Temple…
Built high places for idols.
The Danger of a Divided Heart
Solomon didn’t wake up one morning and say, “Today I’ll betray God.”

You can be gifted.
Anointed.
Publicly successful.
The Bible says, “His heart was not fully devoted to the Lord his God.” (1 Kings 11:4)
The kingdom would split after his death.
The wisest man who ever lived… couldn’t out-think a wandering heart.
Solomon’s drift whispers a greater name.
Because where Solomon failed, another Son of David stood firm.

Tempted—but without sin.
Offered kingdoms—but chose the cross.
Surrounded by broken devotion—but remained faithful unto death.
Solomon built a temple of gold.
Jesus built a living temple with His blood.
Solomon’s divided heart fractured a kingdom.
Jesus’ surrendered heart secured an eternal one.

If you feel the drift…
If your heart is split between God and something glittering…
Repentance is not humiliation. It is homecoming.
The cross is not shame. It is rescue.
You don’t need to be the wisest person in the room.

And the only One who can give you a new heart
is Jesus.
